races.name: Download The At The Races App Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands C And D) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Princess Honey Bee
runners_data.note: Craig Lidster's filly has the clearest role in this field, leading throughout at a pace she dictates; her one win on Standard going (1/6 on similar surface) is directly relevant and Saffie Osborne's low-weight claim is a bonus, though she has placed rather than won on her recent outings.

runners_data.name: All Shall Be Well
runners_data.note: Completely lightly raced with no form string to evaluate, her running style is listed unknown and she carries a conspicuously high OR of 120 — Jason Watson takes the ride for a trainer in decent recent form (2/15 over 14 days), but the absence of any public form makes her genuinely difficult to rate.

runners_data.name: Barbuda Bay
runners_data.note: Roger Teal's hold-up filly has her best recent Lingfield Standard form to call on (3/8f/STA) but her overall record on this surface reads 0 wins 2 places from 7 and she must produce a sustained finish from off the pace in a race unlikely to be run at a searching tempo.

runners_data.name: Mystic Music
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's yard is in strong form (12/63 over 14 days) and Mystic Music ran a solid second over 8f on Good going, but Nicola Currie will need to conjure a late run in a race where the honest pace required to set up closers looks absent.

runners_data.name: Hamdania
runners_data.note: James Horton's filly returns from 271 days off the track having won her only start over 7f on Standard going at Lingfield — course-and-going form is ideal and a prominent position behind the leader suits, though fitness after a nine-month absence is the critical unknown.

races.paceDynamic: Princess Honey Bee is the sole confirmed front-runner and will lead from the gates at a sustainable, uncontested gallop over Lingfield's flat Polytrack mile. Hamdania will push up prominently from stall, likely sitting just off the leader's quarters, while Barbuda Bay and Mystic Music settle further back in hold-up positions. With no rivals able or willing to challenge Princess Honey Bee for the lead, the pace will be controlled and moderate, creating a race run to suit those who can sit handy and sustain their effort into the straight rather than those who must launch from deep. This race shape firmly favours the prominent or lead-tracking profile — horses who can settle within two lengths of the front and exploit the lack of genuine pace pressure in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Princess Honey Bee Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Princess Honey Bee dictates a steady, uncontested gallop and kicks on from the home turn.
scenarios.body: She sets her own fractions throughout, and with no rival able to apply pressure, she converts front-running control into a decisive advantage in the straight; her Standard-going form (1/6 on similar surface) is a direct asset here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hamdania Tracks And Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Hamdania travels prominently behind Princess Honey Bee and produces a decisive turn-of-foot in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Hamdania's sole career run was a win on Standard going over 7f at Lingfield, giving her a perfect course-and-going profile, and sitting second throughout allows her to pounce when the pace softens.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the straight and the hold-up runners get the finish they need.
scenarios.body: Mystic Music's placed effort over 8f on Standard is the most relevant closer form here, and Barbuda Bay would need the front two to tie each other up completely — possible but not the expected tempo shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Upset From Unknown
scenarios.trigger: If All Shall Be Well, lightly raced and carrying an unusually high OR, is significantly better than her rating suggests and outstays rivals late.
scenarios.body: With an OR of 120 on debut context and Jason Watson riding, she cannot be ignored entirely, but unknown style and lightly-raced profile make this a deeply uncertain premise.

watchPoints.text: Hamdania's layoff of 271 days is the single biggest swing factor — watch her in the paddock and monitor how sharply she travels in the first two furlongs, as a fit-enough display tracking Princess Honey Bee could make her a serious threat.

All Shall Be Well's OR of 120 in a Band C/D novice merits attention — if her work at home justifies that figure, she could be dramatically better than anything else in this field despite no public form to examine.
Princess Honey Bee's tendency to place rather than win (form: 34-224) raises a question about whether she converts front-running control into a victory or gets pegged back late by a fresher rival.

With Barbuda Bay and Mystic Music both holding up off a likely steady gallop, watch whether either can find a gear change in the straight — a truly slow early pace would compress the field and reduce the advantage of their late-run style.

races.name: Castle Air Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Big Bear Hug
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer for Jim Boyle whose sole AW Standard win came at a similar trip (12f); Olivia Haines claims 7lb which is meaningful at this level, and his 8-day turnaround after a 6th is routine for the yard — his scenario depends on Romantic Spirit injecting enough pace to bring him into the race late.
runners_data.comment: Big Bear Hug won earlier in the campaign and has experience of both today's trip and going, while carrying 133 lb on a quick turnaround of just eight days; the risk is that her last three runs have yielded a pair of sevenths and a fifth.

runners_data.name: Sibling Rivelry
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of six on our figures and rated just 72, she is hard to fancy despite consecutive runner-up finishes last time out and one start back; has run over today's trip and going, which at least removes those unknowns.

runners_data.name: Romantic Spirit
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and race-shaper; David Menuisier has had no runners in the past 14 days (0/16) and this mare returns after 68 days off having finished 7th in her last three — she controls the fractions but her stamina reservoir late appears compromised by recent results, making her more of a pace-setter than a winner.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with three consecutive seventh-place finishes making her hard to fancy on form, and 68 days off the track adds a fitness query; she has run over today's trip and going before, and a weight of 128 lb gives little encouragement on these figures.

runners_data.name: Mister Daydream
runners_data.note: Gary & Josh Moore have been in form (3/32 T14) and this horse won his last AW Standard start, giving him genuine course-going credentials; he is a true hold-up type whose natural race is run from the back, but with the rear crowded in this field he'll be pressed into midfield — the positional compromise is a real cost to his effectiveness.
runners_data.comment: Mister Daydream boasts a win three starts back and was runner-up two starts back, showing he can compete at this level, and he has experience over today's trip and going; the main risk is a below-par effort last time out after 41 days off.

runners_data.name: Twilight Moon
runners_data.note: Marcus Tregoning's four-year-old runs in headgear (p) and has a course-winning AW Standard run in his recent record (1st, 12f, STA); 35 days since last run is not a concern for this stable and Marco Ghiani will look to slot in just behind the leader — his profile suits the dominant scenario well if he gets a clean run from his draw.
runners_data.comment: Twilight Moon showed her best when winning earlier in recent form, and she has experience of today's trip and conditions — though her third last time out followed back-to-back sixths, and that inconsistency is the chief concern at 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Wiltshire Wonder
runners_data.note: Bernard Llewellyn's six-year-old returns after 82 days — the longest break in the field — and Ryan Kavanagh takes the 3lb claim; his AW Standard record shows a win at 12f and he is a hold-up type who needs a true gallop, meaning his chance is directly tied to whether Romantic Spirit stretches the field sufficiently.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and absent for 82 days, Wiltshire Wonder nonetheless heads the field on our ratings and has experience of today's distance and going; at 135 lb he will need to find plenty, but the form figures hint at ability waiting to be unlocked.

races.paceDynamic: Romantic Spirit is the sole confirmed front-runner in a six-runner field and should lead from the outset on Standard Lingfield AW, controlling tempo from the front without meaningful pressure — her recent form shows seven finishes between 4th and 7th, but she has exceptional course familiarity with 13 starts on this surface. Sibling Rivalry and Twilight Moon are the genuine prominent types who will contest the early positions directly behind her, creating a defined two-tier formation with the hold-up horses — Big Bear Hug, Wiltshire Wonder, and the redistributed Mister Daydream — settled further back. This field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear, and Mister Daydream, a natural hold-up horse, has been mapped to midfield due to crowding at the back, meaning he is unlikely to operate from his truest position. With one uncontested pace-setter and a genuine two-length+ gap to the midfield-plus group, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can sit just off the leader, conserve energy through the long 1m4f trip, and deliver a decisive move from 3f out — making the P-style profile the primary beneficiary.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Romantic Spirit Leads; Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Romantic Spirit controls a steady, uncontested gallop and the prominent pair track her into the straight.
scenarios.body: Sibling Rivalry and Twilight Moon sit just off the leader's shoulder through the final bend and are best-placed to challenge as she inevitably fades; their proximity to the pace at a distance that suits their profiles gives them first run on everything behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Ups Unleash Late
scenarios.trigger: If Romantic Spirit sets a genuinely strong gallop that burns off the prominent pair and leaves the race wide open late.
scenarios.body: Big Bear Hug and Wiltshire Wonder, both proven closers with winning form on AW Standard, pick up the pieces in the final furlong if the pace has been genuinely searching; Big Bear Hug's 1m1f AW win and Wiltshire Wonder's course winning form give them the finishing profile to capitalise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Leader Stays On; Upsets
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so moderate that Romantic Spirit coasts and finds energy reserves to hold on into the straight.
scenarios.body: Romantic Spirit has strong course familiarity (13 AW starts) and could theoretically sustain a soft-set tempo well enough to hold off tired chasers; this is a low-probability outcome given her recent string of 7th-place finishes, but moderate pace and a big drop in field size makes it non-negligible.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Mister Daydream Overturns Map
scenarios.trigger: If Mister Daydream, despite being displaced from his natural hold-up position, settles comfortably in midfield and produces a strong staying run.
scenarios.body: This scenario is discounted because the STYLE_FIT tag confirms he is racing materially out of role, making it less likely he delivers his best effort; his AW form (2nd and 1st on Standard) gives him underlying ability, but the positional compromise weakens his chance meaningfully relative to true-shaped rivals.

watchPoints.text: Romantic Spirit's true pace — if she rolls along without being pressured she may set a crawl that undermines the hold-up runners completely; watch the opening 2f sectional to judge whether this is a genuine test.

Twilight Moon's headgear (first-time or re-applied visor) could sharpen his early response and see him push closer to the leader than expected — monitor his position at the first bend as it determines whether Sibling Rivalry has a rival to race against.

Mister Daydream has been mapped to midfield despite being a natural hold-up horse; if he fails to settle in that enforced position he could run a flat race, dragging perceived market confidence with him for no reward.

Big Bear Hug's 7lb claimer Olivia Haines reduces the burden to an effective 126lbs — the lightest in the field — which could prove a marginal edge in a staying handicap over 1m4f if the pace scenario suits late runners.

Wiltshire Wonder's 82-day layoff is the most significant absence in the race; Bernard Llewellyn's yard runs returnees competently (1/12 T14) but a first run back over this trip on AW after a break from soft ground warrants monitoring in running before concluding he is at peak readiness.

races.name: Free Tips On attheraces.com Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Forager
runners_data.note: Dual course winner (5f Standard) in recent form but a natural hold-up horse who will be denied his preferred position in this slow-tempo race; Simon Pearce's 0/2 last 14 days is a minor concern and the style mismatch is the primary drag on his chance.
runners_data.comment: Forager showed she can win at this level when scoring four starts back, and she has experience of today's distance and going to call upon from stall six carrying 137 lb. The risk is her more recent string of finishes outside the frame.

runners_data.name: Wyle Cop
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins at Lingfield over 5f on Standard give him a standout course profile, and Jason Watson is a shrewd booking; his hold-up style becomes less of an issue if he is positioned handily off the lone leader, making him the principal danger to Diomed Duke.
runners_data.comment: Wyle Cop has won twice in his last six starts, most recently 19 days ago, and has experience over today's trip and going, but our rating ranks him fifth of six in this field, making him hard to fancy at this level despite that recent winning momentum.

runners_data.name: Diomed Duke
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field, giving him an uncontested lead and the ability to control tempo entirely; wears a tongue-tie, trained by Stuart Williams who is 2/31 over 14 days, and the 7lb claimer Olivia Haines is a watch factor, but his tactical advantage is substantial on a flat 5f AW track.
runners_data.comment: Diomed Duke arrives in fine fettle after just 12 days, boasting a win two starts back and a third last time out, and he has experience of both today's trip and conditions; the main threat to his claims is carrying 134 lb from stall 2.

runners_data.name: Truly Glamorous
runners_data.note: Showed smart form winning twice on Good ground earlier this season but has since regressed; a genuine hold-up performer who will be shuffled closer than she likes here, and 35 days off adds a small fitness query for Christopher Mason's yard which is 0/5 in the last fortnight.
runners_data.comment: Two wins in his last five starts show Truly Glamorous can find the winner's enclosure, but ranked last of six on our figures and carrying 129 lb, he faces a stiff task, though he has run over today's trip and the recent winning form offers slim encouragement.

runners_data.name: Noble Vow
runners_data.note: Has winning form on AW (Firestone) and has shown pace on Standard going; his Hannon yard is in a quiet 14-day spell (0/43) and recent form figures include back-to-back poor runs at Goodwood, but his tactical versatility gives him an each-way claim if the pace is truly modest.
runners_data.comment: Boasts back-to-back wins three and four starts back, and has experience of today's trip and conditions; he carries a hefty 137 lb from stall 3, and his last two runs were unplaced, so he needs to bounce back, but the form underneath makes him the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Toolatetonegotiate
runners_data.note: Three wins from nine starts at 5f, including two on Good ground, and Daisy Hitchins' yard is in fair form; primarily a hold-up horse who benefits most from a strong gallop, but that is the one ingredient missing here — he will be forced closer than ideal and Millie Wonnacott's 5lb claim only partially compensates.
runners_data.comment: Toolatetonegotiate showed a progressive profile when winning and finishing second and third in earlier starts, and her experience over today's trip and going is a clear asset carrying 137 lb from stall 5; the main risk is her disappointing back-to-back efforts since that win.

races.paceDynamic: Diomed Duke is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner 5f sprint on Lingfield's Polytrack, and with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, he can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the gates. The remainder of the field — Wyle Cop, Noble Vow, Forager, Truly Glamorous, and Toolatetonegotiate — are all hold-up or prominent types, meaning the pace is unlikely to be pressured or artificially strong, reducing the chance of a true end-to-end test. This field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate: Toolatetonegotiate, Forager, and Truly Glamorous are genuine closers who will be forced closer to the pace than they ideally prefer, compromising their trademark late runs. A controlled, single-pacemaker race on 5f at Lingfield AW strongly favours horses who can race handily off a modest gallop and quicken in the straight — the prominent-to-midfield profile with tactical speed is the profile to be on here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Diomed Duke Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Diomed Duke breaks cleanly and settles into his own rhythm without any challenger harassing him through the early stages.
scenarios.body: Diomed Duke sets a comfortable tempo that is fast enough to string the field out but controlled enough to preserve his finishing effort, leaving those tracking wide in his wake with too much ground to make up in the short Lingfield straight. On Standard AW at this trip, his course-and-distance form and front-running role make him the hardest horse to pass once he has stolen a length advantage at halfway.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Diomed Duke is unable to quicken in the closing stages and the compressed hold-up pack produces a late surge that catches him on the line.
scenarios.body: A steady gallop paradoxically risks giving genuine hold-up horses a short, sharp sprint rather than a grind, allowing Wyle Cop or Noble Vow — who have both scored on this surface — to come from just off the pace and cut him down inside the final furlong. Wyle Cop's back-to-back Lingfield wins and Noble Vow's winning form on AW make both dangerous if the race pans out with a late rush.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse like Wyle Cop or Noble Vow tracks Diomed Duke closely enough to pounce at the two-furlong pole when the leader's stride shortens.
scenarios.body: Rather than a late swooping finish, the race is decided by a horse sitting second or third, matching the leader stride for stride before edging ahead in the final 100 yards. Wyle Cop's consistent recent form — two straight wins at this course and distance — fits this profile precisely, and the jockey booking of Jason Watson underlines connections' confidence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Closers Land Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up brigade — Toolatetonegotiate, Forager, or Truly Glamorous — manage to find clear running and sustain a finishing effort despite racing closer than they prefer.
scenarios.body: These three horses are all true hold-up types forced into a midfield role by the race's limited pace supply, making it harder for them to produce their best with fewer rivals ahead to weave through. Their style-fit discounts are significant, and only an unusually strong pace collapse or a chaotic early split would create enough daylight for one of them to arrive late with a winning run.

watchPoints.text: Diomed Duke's early break is critical — if Olivia Haines (7lb claimer) allows him to drift wide or miss the kick, the entire pace plan collapses and the race shape shifts dramatically.
Wyle Cop has won twice here over this trip on Standard and is most likely to track Diomed Duke into a challenging position — watch whether Jason Watson commits early or waits for the straight.

Toolatetonegotiate, Forager, and Truly Glamorous are all genuine closers forced to race closer than their natural style — if all three sit in a bunch behind the leader, a traffic problem in the short straight is a real possibility.
The Standard AW surface at Lingfield on this card has been consistent all afternoon — no bias reports suggest pace advantage is amplified, keeping the race shape assessment clean.

Noble Vow's last two starts on Good at Goodwood produced figures of 17th and 12th — the switch back to AW Standard removes that ground concern, and his previous AW form (won on Fibresand) is worth noting if the race unfolds with a late dash.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 / EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Kss De Triomphe Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Lost In Wonder
runners_data.note: A hold-up performer for Camilla Poulton who has been off 122 days — the lengthy absence is a significant concern at 2m on AW Standard, and her best recent form at 7-8f raises a genuine stamina question over this trip; Tom Queally will need to settle her well to have any chance.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and returning after a 122-day absence, Lost In Wonder faces a stiff ask off 140 lb, though she has experience of today's going and a second four starts back hints at ability that has since proved elusive.

runners_data.name: Further Measure
runners_data.note: Mike Murphy's nine-year-old has strong course form (14 of 15 runs on Standard going) and wears a hood, but his natural style is hold-up — he only leads here by default in the absence of any other pace, so he races entirely out of his preferred mode and the style-fit discount applies.|
runners_data.comment: Further Measure has experience of today's distance and going, and a win in his last six starts gives him a clear profile to work from; our rating puts him at the head of this field, though he has work to do to recapture that winning form after five modest efforts.

runners_data.name: Charles Morin
runners_data.note: Pat Phelan's five-year-old won over 12f on Standard recently and wears a blinker, suggesting he needs driving out; though his true role is hold-up, he is shown in midfield and carries a STYLE_FIT of 0.92, so his best chance comes if the tempo is genuinely strong enough for closers to get home.|
runners_data.comment: Charles Morin returns here in good heart after winning last time out, and his experience over today's trip and conditions is a clear asset at 133 lb; the main risk is that his two runs before that victory yielded unplaced efforts, raising questions about consistency.

runners_data.name: Ada Rose
runners_data.note: Kevin Philippart De Foy's three-year-old has a course-and-distance win to her name (1/12f/STA) and Jack Mitchell is a strong booking; she is a natural hold-up filly pushed into a midfield map position, and her proven ability to win on this surface at today's trip makes her the most credentialed closer in the field.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten in five of her last six starts, with only a win two starts back offering any encouragement, Ada Rose ranks second-bottom on our figures here and faces a stiff ask, though she has run over today's going before and returns on a reasonable 30-day break.

runners_data.name: Fabled Spirit
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's three-year-old is flagged for fading in the finish — a warning that carries real weight over 2m — and her best recent run came over 16f on Standard; Gina Mangan rides and the headgear note (p) shows Watson is trying to find a switch, but the stamina concern is hard to ignore.|
runners_data.comment: Fabled Spirit has finished placed in each of his last two starts and returns here in good heart after 26 days, with experience of today's trip and conditions working in his favour, though his lack of a win in recent starts is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Sir Griflet
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha's three-year-old has never won or placed in nine Standard-going runs (0W0P), wears a tongue-tie and cheekpieces, and has been well beaten in similar company recently; Saffie Osborne picks up the ride but the form figures over 12-16f on this surface offer little encouragement.|
runners_data.comment: Sir Griflet has run over today's trip and going before and, rated 61 against a field of seven, shapes as a leading player; the worry is that he has been winless in his last six starts, with a fourth his best recent showing.

runners_data.name: Romeo's Guardian
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's three-year-old is flagged for fading in the finish and has recorded 0W0P across five runs on Standard going; most of his career has been at 6-10f and the step up to 2m looks a very significant ask, with Connor Planas unable to disguise the lack of any staying credentials in the form book.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with finishes no better than seventh in that spell, Romeo's Guardian is hard to fancy ranked bottom of the field on our figures, though he returns on a quick turnaround and has experience of today's going.

races.paceDynamic: Further Measure is the lone confirmed pace-setter here, redistributed to the front despite being a natural hold-up horse, meaning this 2m Lingfield AW contest is likely to be run at a sustainable, uncontested tempo with no genuine pressure applied early. With seven runners and a field dominated by true hold-up types — Ada Rose, Sir Griflet, Fabled Spirit, Charles Morin and Romeo's Guardian all natural closers compressed into the midfield on the map — the race shape is likely to be strung out in a patient, single-file procession rather than a tactical scrap. The field holds considerably more hold-up and prominent types than can physically get their preferred positions, with Further Measure most likely to lead by default and perhaps Charles Morin or Ada Rose pushing into closer contact given their recent form at this distance. A controlled, steady gallop over 2m that suits closers with a genuine staying kick is the dominant shape, favouring horses who can travel efficiently in midfield and produce a sustained late run rather than those needing a truly searching pace to peg back a front-runner.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Further Measure sets an uncontested, even gallop and the race only quickens entering the straight.
scenarios.body: Further Measure dictates a measured tempo unchallenged, leaving plenty of runners travelling well in behind before the home turn triggers a bunched finish; horses with a genuine finishing kick over this trip thrive.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Further Measure, racing out of natural role, nonetheless relaxes beautifully and proves good enough to hold on from the front.
scenarios.body: A slow-burn pace with Further Measure controlling the fractions can become a front-runner's race if pursuers fail to pick up in time over this long 2m trip; the lack of a genuine pace rival means no one has the incentive to attack until too late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Fail To Quicken
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so moderate that the entire field arrives at the two-furlong pole in a heap and the race becomes a sprint.
scenarios.body: A falsely slow early gallop can paradoxically favour horses with tactical speed and the ability to quicken from a handy position rather than true stayers grinding it out; runners carried wide or unable to find a run suffer.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Grinds Field
scenarios.trigger: If a quirk in fractions or a runner attempting to stretch the field mid-race turns this into a genuine stamina examination.
scenarios.body: A more genuinely run 2m would expose any horse lacking resolution and reward those with proven staying pedigree and strong finishing records at this trip; horses who fade in the finish under this scenario are immediately disadvantaged.

watchPoints.text: Further Measure — watch whether he actually settles into a sensible lead rhythm or fights for his head; if he races keenly out of role, he could burn out the field's pace reserves unexpectedly and dramatically alter the shape.|

Ada Rose — Jack Mitchell's positioning in the first half-mile is critical; if she gets shuffled too far back in a small, slow-run field she may never land a telling blow despite having the best course-and-distance form.|

Fabled Spirit and Romeo's Guardian — both are flagged as horses who fade in the finish, and a 2m trip on a fair surface with no pace pressure to compress the race is the worst possible scenario for either; watch for them to get outpaced from the two-furlong pole.|

Charles Morin — his blinker application suggests the yard wants more early commitment, and if he forces his way to a handy position rather than dropping in last, the true midfield map position could actually reflect where he ends up rather than being a redistribution quirk.|

races.name: Csis - Neigh Nonsense Insurance Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Sugar Sugar
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly in good recent form (1-2 at Lingfield AW over 6f on Standard), steps up to 7f here which is a slight query but her dam-side suggests it will suit; George Bass takes over and she carried 133lbs well last time, though being a natural backmarker in a field of closers means she will need a strong pace and a clean run.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom but one on our figures and with just one win in her last five starts, Sugar Sugar is hard to fancy at the weights, though she has run over today's trip and going before and that recent victory two starts back shows she can find the line.

runners_data.name: Hamaleel
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with a very strong Lingfield AW profile (10 runs here, 1W 6P), has placed five times at 7f/Standard — Conor Whiteley's 5lb claim is useful; needs a true gallop to come through late and this modest pace scenario suits her less than it might look.
runners_data.comment: Hamaleel shaped with promise when third two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, giving her solid claims here from stall three; the main concern is that she remains winless in her last six starts, suggesting the winning chance may just elude her again.

runners_data.name: Dark Brunette
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old whose form is hard to assess fully (just one run on Standard going); George Wood rides for the in-form Jane Chapple-Hyam yard (1/10 last 14 days) and that third at Lingfield AW over 6f on Standard is solid bedrock — the step to 7f is the key unknown, and the U (unknown style) tag means tactical positioning is genuinely uncertain.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and a second twice in her last five starts, Dark Brunette is winless in recent starts but shows consistent placing ability; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 17 days between runs leaves her fit enough to go again from stall 5.

runners_data.name: Searchingtheblues
runners_data.note: Gina Mangan partners this mare who is a genuine deep hold-up type at heart — placed 13 times from 15 on similar going, but dropped back to 7f from 8f trips most recently; her natural rearward position is harder to execute in a field this loaded with closers, reducing the probability she gets the strong, honest gallop she needs to deliver.
runners_data.comment: Searchingtheblues arrives here just 13 days after finishing second last time out, and her experience over today's trip and going is a useful platform, but she remains yet to win in her last six starts and carries 132 lb from stall six, with a third three starts back her only other notable effort.

runners_data.name: Lili Marleen
runners_data.note: Has a poor recent record including a fall and a pulled-up — the fades-in-finish flag is a concern, and her Standard-going figures (just 1W1P from 6 runs) are modest; she is a true hold-up mare whose position in the race map is squeezed by the volume of backmarkers, making a clean passage extremely unlikely.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with a fell and a pulled up among the recent blemishes, Lili Marleen looks hard to fancy from stall seven on a rating of 54, though she has run over today's distance and going before and a 15-day turnaround suggests she arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Espanita
runners_data.note: Won over this exact trip and surface (7f/Lingfield AW/Standard) last time out for Charlie Johnston, giving her strong credentials on paper; however, she is a natural hold-up horse with a style-fit flag, and in a race where she cannot sit where she wants, her ability to reproduce that win is compromised — the big Johnston yard is 5/40 over 14 days, a healthy strike rate worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Espanita won two starts back but has otherwise struggled for consistency, finishing sixth last time out and out of the frame in five of her last six, and our rating ranks her eighth of ten here, making her hard to fancy despite the distance and going experience.

runners_data.name: Angels' Share
runners_data.note: Marco Ghiani takes the ride on this three-year-old who has placed at 7f/Standard twice this season; she is a genuine backmarker whose last two course wins (both on AW) suggest the surface suits, but the crowded hold-up sector means she will be competing for the same space as five other closers — her best chance is a stronger-than-expected pace developing.
runners_data.comment: Twice third in her last two starts, Angels' Share arrives on a fresh 17-day break with distance and going experience in her favour, yet she remains winless in recent starts and a mark of 64 combined with 130 lb from stall ten leaves her with plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Daisy Roots
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with an outstanding record at Lingfield AW over 7f (10/15 on similar going, 1W 3P) who maps naturally prominent for Jim Boyle — she has finished 4th-4th-4th on her last three visits here, suggesting she is running into form; a 30-day break is not a concern given Boyle's patient handling, and her position just behind Ironist is the ideal racing spot in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Daisy Roots none the less arrives fresh on 30 days' rest, carrying 135 lb from stall one, and has run over today's distance and going before — her overall profile, including a rating of 71, makes her our preferred pick here.

runners_data.name: Ironist
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner, tagged with a style-fit flag because she runs sometimes more prominently than the race shape demands, but here she has every reason to relax — she can stride to the front unchallenged, set whatever pace she chooses, and get first run in the Lingfield AW straight; 57 days off is the only minor flag, but George Margarson's record suggests horses return fit.
runners_data.comment: Ironist has run over today's trip and going, and her rating of 70 edges her official mark, suggesting she retains ability — the main risk is that she has been winless in her last five starts and returns after 57 days off.

runners_data.name: Cixi
runners_data.note: Jack Mitchell takes over for Jim Boyle on this OR-68 topweight who steps back to 7f after a 10f try; her best Lingfield result was a 3rd at 7f/Standard so the trip and surface combination is known to suit — she is a hold-up filly who will need to find a gap in a congested finish, and 38 days since her last run means fitness is a fair query.
runners_data.comment: Ranked top of ten on our rating, Cixi arrives here with distance and going experience to call on, and her third-placed effort four starts back shows she can mix it at this level — yet winless in her last five starts and a seventh last time out, she must bounce back sharply.

races.paceDynamic: Ironist is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner 7f Lingfield AW handicap and, with no genuine pace rival to press her, Saffie Osborne can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front — precisely the kind of uncontested lead that makes life very comfortable for a prominent racer. Daisy Roots is the only other horse mapping naturally to a prominent position, meaning she can tuck in just behind Ironist and also benefit from a well-structured, unfrenetic pace. This field is heavily loaded with hold-up types — Searchingtheblues, Lili Marleen, Espanita, Angels' Share, Sugar Sugar, Hamaleel and Cixi all want to come from off the pace — but there are far more of them than the race shape can accommodate cleanly, so some will inevitably be shuffled wider or hemmed in on a track where the home straight at Lingfield AW rewards those who find a clear run early in the straight. The race shape strongly favours front-running and prominent-racing profiles: a measured pace set by Ironist will compress the race and leave hold-up horses with a shorter, flatter run-in than they need, making it hardest for the redistributed closers to deliver their true form.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ironist Controls, Front Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If Ironist bowls along uncontested at a fair but not gruelling gallop, dictating every fraction.
scenarios.body: Saffie Osborne settles Ironist into a rhythm with Daisy Roots tracking closely, and the lack of early pressure means the pace is never truly searching enough to bring the closers into play by the home turn. Front-running and prominent types get first run on the straight rail and the gap is never bridged.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Cavalry Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves more honest than expected and the closers get a strong enough gallop to aim at.
scenarios.body: Several of the redistributed hold-up horses — Searchingtheblues, Espanita or Cixi — find a gap on the inside rail turning in and the sustained gallop at 7f stretches Ironist in the final furlong. This scenario is discounted because the hold-up contingent is larger than the race can correctly place, raising the risk of traffic, and none of them is a natural sit-and-sprint type in this configuration.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Daisy Roots or another handy type tracks Ironist and finds extra when it matters most.
scenarios.body: Daisy Roots has outstanding course form at Lingfield AW over 7f, travels prominently and can challenge Ironist inside the final two furlongs if the front-runner has given her all early. A race run at a steady pace that becomes a sprint from two out suits a horse with a powerful finishing kick from a handy position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Wide-Open Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Ironist goes off too quickly and ties up, causing a contested late scramble across the field.
scenarios.body: Without a strong pace-enforcer in behind, Ironist occasionally over-racks herself in front, and if she fades sharply in the final furlong a late-into-it horse such as Hamaleel — who has strong Lingfield AW course form at this trip — could benefit from the ensuing chaos. This remains a low-probability outcome because Ironist's likely uncontested lead means there is no reason for her to over-race.

watchPoints.text: Ironist — if she gets a completely uncontested lead and the pace is this controlled, Saffie Osborne could dictate every fraction and prove very difficult to peg back in the Lingfield straight.

Traffic risk for the hold-up cluster — Searchingtheblues, Espanita, Angels' Share, Sugar Sugar, Hamaleel and Cixi all want to come from behind, so watch for crowding and interference on the home turn as they all attempt to find daylight simultaneously.
Daisy Roots — her course record at this exact trip is the best in the field; if Ironist fades at all inside the final furlong, Daisy Roots is positioned to pounce and has done it before here.

Espanita — won over this exact course, distance and going last time, so the form is highly relevant, but her style-fit tag and the overcrowded hold-up sector mean backers should check the early market move carefully for any confidence signal from the Johnston camp.

Dark Brunette — the Chapple-Hyam yard is live (1/10 last 14 days), this filly's style is genuinely unknown, and a lightly raced three-year-old stepping up in trip on a surface she has placed on before can outrun a big price if the pace unfolds favourably.

races.name: Get Raceday Ready Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Come On Over
runners_data.note: Demonstrated sharp form with a recent Goodwood win and a near-miss second, so the ability is live — but this horse's natural inclination is to race from the rear, and in a field stacked with hold-up types it will struggle to find that position, meaning it races somewhat against its grain here under Conor Whiteley (5lb claim).
runners_data.comment: Come On Over has winning form in his last six starts, landing the spoils most recently and again three back, and at 12 days he arrives here fit and fresh; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 134 lb from stall seven is the hand he plays.

runners_data.name: Bucklow Hill
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner and the structural pivot of this entire shape — Jason Watson can take an uncontested lead, dictate on Standard Lingfield AW (sole win was on this surface), and his 42-day break on a horse trained by the in-form Charles Hills unit (3/21 in 14 days) carries no obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Watchdog
runners_data.note: Returned to winning form on soft ground at Goodwood most recently and again on Good, showing he handles varying conditions, but 99 days off is notable and his instinct to race from the back of the field will be frustrated in a race where so many rivals share the same tactical preference, with J F Egan needing to be creative about positioning.
runners_data.comment: Watchdog won two of his last five starts, including back-to-back victories two and three starts back, but a sixth last time out and 99 days off the track are questions he must answer; has run over today's trip and going, and 133 lb is no featherweight assignment.

runners_data.name: Pilgrim's Progress
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's 3-year-old has placed on Standard AW ground twice and can race prominently, making this a genuinely more natural fit in the pace map than most of his rivals; Alec Voikhansky takes the ride with Hannon's yard in a quiet 14-day spell (0/43) which tempers confidence, but the horse's profile suits the expected race shape well.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Pilgrim's Progress is hard to fancy despite the second two starts back and experience over today's trip and going; a trainer without a strike from 43 runners in the past fortnight compounds the concern.

runners_data.name: Go Lockers Go
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's runner has shown consistent placed form including AW wins and places at Standard, and George Wood's booking is straightforward — the issue is that this horse's true style is hold-up, and with multiple rivals wanting the same rear-of-field territory, it will find itself racing closer than ideal without necessarily having the pace-shape to exploit it.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out keeps Go Lockers Go in the picture, and he has experience over today's trip and conditions, while our rating of 78 underlines his claims as a genuine threat; the main risk is that his one win in his last six starts suggests he can be hard to win with.

runners_data.name: Far Too Fizzy
runners_data.note: The most AW-experienced runner in the field with 14 of 15 career runs on similar going, giving Laura Pearson a mount that clearly handles the surface — but racing just 2 days after its last run is unusual, and as another horse whose natural position is off the pace, it enters the same crowded tactical space as several rivals here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Far Too Fizzy is hard to fancy, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns third last time out as a mild crumb of comfort — the concern is whether two days between runs leaves him fully wound up.

runners_data.name: Acclaimed Freedom
runners_data.note: George Scott's charge arrives on fair form with two recent AW placed efforts at 6f Standard, and Marco Ghiani is a strong booking on this track — Acclaimed Freedom can race with some tactical flexibility, sitting in behind the pace without needing to be at the very back, which gives it a marginally better chance of finding a workable position than the confirmed hold-up types.
runners_data.comment: Acclaimed Freedom arrives here in fine order, second last time out and a second four starts back, with experience of today's trip and going working in his favour and our rating of 82 marking him as a serious threat; the risk is that he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Romeo Montague
runners_data.note: A 210-day absence since finishing fifth on this course and distance is a significant fitness question, and Saffie Osborne will be managing a fresh horse rather than one in a rhythm — on form it has won at 6f Standard (Lingfield) and placed at Goodwood, so the ability is there, but the layoff alone makes this a speculative runner in any scenario.
runners_data.comment: Romeo Montague shaped with plenty of promise when winning three starts back, and he brings distance and going experience alongside a top-ranked profile that marks him out as a genuine threat here; the concern is a 210-day absence since his last outing.

races.paceDynamic: Bucklow Hill is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should slide into an uncontested position from the outset, controlling tempo from the front on what is a Standard Lingfield AW surface over 6f. This is a genuinely pace-light race at the front end — Bucklow Hill can dictate a sustainable, honest gallop without ever being pressured, which on this track and going strongly favours a horse that can quicken from a position of comfort rather than one needing a scorching pace to deliver a late charge. The field contains a surplus of hold-up types — Come On Over, Watchdog, Go Lockers Go, and Far Too Fizzy are all natural rear-runners redistributed into midfield on the map because they cannot all find their preferred position — meaning the race shape is most likely to reward Bucklow Hill on the front end or a genuinely prominent runner like Pilgrim's Progress who can track and pounce. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape favours front-running or close-tracking prominence profiles, with true hold-up horses at a structural disadvantage unless the pace collapses late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bucklow Hill Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Bucklow Hill leads from the front without any pressure and controls a fair but not punishing tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Bucklow Hill settles into a rhythm on the front end, burns off nothing early, and has enough in reserve to repel challenges in the final furlong on Standard AW ground; prominent trackers like Pilgrim's Progress are the main dangers but face a horse that has never been forced to race hard. This shape entirely suits an uncontested pace-setter on a track where controlling leaders have a strong record, especially at 6f where the straight allows a timed kick.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If a close-tracking horse sits just off Bucklow Hill's pace and produces a stronger finish in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Pilgrim's Progress or Acclaimed Freedom, both capable of racing prominently, latch onto Bucklow Hill's pace through the first half and deliver their effort from a position of coverage rather than a wide sweeping run; the modest early pace means the finish is a contest of quality rather than stamina, slightly opening the door for the best-rated horses. This shape rewards the horse with the highest cruising speed sitting second or third, rather than one relying on late gas from well off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop quickens enough to string the field out and allow a genuinely late-running horse to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires Bucklow Hill to set a stronger-than-expected tempo, leaving enough attrition for Come On Over, Watchdog, or Far Too Fizzy to finish through beaten horses — but given all three are redistributed from their natural hold-up berth, none will be as far back as they'd prefer, blunting the late thrust they'd typically generate. Far Too Fizzy brings significant AW course experience (14/15 runs on similar going) and Come On Over's recent win at Goodwood gives form claims, but both face a structural disadvantage in this pace scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Pace Collapses
scenarios.trigger: If Bucklow Hill sets too slow a pace and the field bunches, turning the race into a sprint finish from the 2f pole.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run race would theoretically open things up for any runner, but there is no secondary pace force to inject urgency and the rider on Bucklow Hill has every incentive to maintain a measured rhythm; a collapse into a sprint suits a horse with raw speed but this field lacks an obvious standout speedster in those conditions. Romeo Montague, returning from 210 days off, is the wildcard here — fresh horses can sometimes benefit from a messy, speed-dependent finish — but the long absence is a significant concern.

watchPoints.text: Bucklow Hill jumps cleanly from its draw — if it leads within the first furlong unopposed, the race is effectively set and no rival can manufacture pressure without burning themselves out.

Come On Over, Watchdog, Go Lockers Go, and Far Too Fizzy cannot all settle where they want — watch the early stages for crowding and jostling in the rear-midfield group as these hold-up horses compete for position, which could cause traffic problems approaching the home straight.

Romeo Montague is 210 days off the track and any sign of sluggishness or greenness leaving the stalls under Saffie Osborne would immediately confirm it is not a live factor today regardless of its course-winning form.

Pilgrim's Progress is the one prominent-style tracker most likely to have a clear, unobstructed run behind Bucklow Hill — if it travels smoothly through the first half, it becomes the most natural danger to the leader from two furlongs out.

races.name: Air Ambulance Charity Kent Surrey Sussex Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Muy Muy Loco
runners_data.note: Won at 10f on Standard going 14 days ago in good form, but this is a genuine hold-up horse whose natural late-running style is compromised here — with several closers competing for the same rear ground, finding a clear run through a small field on AW is a key tactical risk.
runners_data.comment: Muy Muy Loco won four starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, arriving here fresh on a 14-day break carrying 134 lb from stall 3; the risk is that he has gone unplaced in his last two outings.

runners_data.name: Haveagobeau
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle runner with two wins from five recent starts on Good ground, though Standard AW figures are weaker (9/15); true hold-up style means this horse ideally needs a stronger pace than The Bay Warrior is likely to set, and a Jack Dace claim only partially compensates for the tactical disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and carrying a hefty 132 lb from stall seven, Haveagobeau is hard to fancy at face value, though he has shown he can win in recent starts and has experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Lady Of Clover
runners_data.note: George Scott's lightly-weighted three-year-old has won twice recently including at 12f on Standard, giving her the most relevant form in the race; races from the rear but has shown the ability to quicken, and at 3lb claimed by Liam Wright she holds the profile most likely to bridge the gap to the leaders if the pace is moderate.
runners_data.comment: Rated below her official mark and ranked sixth of seven on our figures, Lady Of Clover is hard to fancy at the weights, though she does arrive in form — a winner last time out and again four starts back — and has run over today's going before.

runners_data.name: Boston Run
runners_data.note: The only genuine prominent-style horse behind The Bay Warrior, giving Marco Ghiani a straightforward stalking position just off the leader; form figures of 0-6642 are modest and he has failed to win from 15 starts on similar going, suggesting he may not have enough class to capitalise even from an ideal tactical spot.
runners_data.comment: Boston Run has been knocking on the door, finishing second last time out after a string of moderate efforts, and he has run over today's trip and going before — the concern is that he remains winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Celtic Spirit
runners_data.note: Goes in blinkers (hg:p) and has zero wins or places from eight starts on Standard AW, which is a significant surface concern; a true hold-up horse shuffled back among several closers, and the headgear switch is the main reason to give any consideration at all.
runners_data.comment: Celtic Spirit has shown glimpses of ability, finishing second twice in recent starts, yet has been winless in his last five and that seventh last time out is a concern; experience over today's trip and going helps, but he carries 130 lb from stall five with little in hand on ratings.

runners_data.name: Saliko
runners_data.note: Saffie Osborne takes over on a horse carrying 136lbs with six recent runs all producing a placed finish of 4th or worse and just 3/15 on similar going — very little to recommend here tactically or on form, and top weight is an additional burden in a moderate contest.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Saliko heads into this rated highly on a speed figure of 65 and our assessment has her narrowly top of the ratings, though consistent placed form has eluded her of late; fresh enough at 17 days since her last run, she has experience over today's trip and conditions from stall six carrying 136 lb.

runners_data.name: The Bay Warrior
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old returning after a 67-day absence for Mark Usher, but the freshness angle is interesting given his excellent Standard-going record (14/15); clear front-runner with no rival for the lead, though the STYLE_FIT tag reflects that he has recently raced more prominently than as an outright leader — the key question is whether he can sustain his advantage over 10 furlongs.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, The Bay Warrior nonetheless shaped with promise when second two runs back, and has experience of today's trip and conditions; the concern is that seventh last time out after a 67-day break leaves his current form open to question.

races.paceDynamic: The Bay Warrior is the lone confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner 1m2f handicap and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will be able to dictate a controlled, unhurried gallop from the front on Standard Lingfield AW. Boston Run is the only other prominent-style runner and will likely settle just off The Bay Warrior's shoulder, meaning the pace is unlikely to be anything more than moderate — creating a sit-and-sprint dynamic over the final two furlongs. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate: Muy Muy Loco, Haveagobeau, Celtic Spirit, and Saliko are all true closers, but with Lady Of Clover also racing from the rear, several of these will be competing for the same ground late and will not get their ideal run. This race shape — a lone front-runner setting a sustainable pace with no pressure — strongly favours prominent racers who can track close to the tempo and pick off the leader, rather than hold-up horses who will face a wall of horses to pass with limited late momentum generated.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bay Warrior Controls And Wins
scenarios.trigger: If The Bay Warrior dictates a comfortable solo lead throughout and the hold-up brigade fail to generate sufficient late momentum.
scenarios.body: The Bay Warrior, uncontested on a Standard surface where he has course form (14/15 similar-going runs), sets his own fractions and quickens at the two-furlong pole before the closers can mount a challenge; Boston Run, tracking in second, is best placed to chase but may lack the class to overhaul a fresh leader (67 days off — fresh angle). This scenario heavily favours The Bay Warrior's front-running profile and Boston Run's prominent tracking position, as the hold-up horses are racing out of their natural roles and face a bunched late charge with too little pace to aim at.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Picks Up Late
scenarios.trigger: If The Bay Warrior sets a pace that just flattens in the final furlong, allowing Boston Run or Lady Of Clover to reel him in.
scenarios.body: Boston Run, tracking in third or fourth, gets a dream run through on the inside rail as The Bay Warrior's effort fades entering the final furlong; Lady Of Clover, who has won twice at this sort of trip on Standard going, is capable of picking up sharply if she can get clear daylight from her hold-up position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If The Bay Warrior over-commits early, the pace lifts sufficiently to set up a strong late finish for one of the genuine closers.
scenarios.body: Haveagobeau or Muy Muy Loco, both with genuine hold-up profiles and solid recent form on similar going, find the gaps in the final furlong to run through; this scenario requires a faster-than-expected gallop to create enough momentum for true closers, which is unlikely given the race has only one front-runner and several redistibuted hold-up types competing for the same late ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Race, Saliko Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If positional jostling among the closers creates trouble and a lightly-raced runner finds a clean passage.
scenarios.body: Saliko, carrying top weight of 136lbs and with a poor recent form string, would need significant improvement and a chaotic race to get involved; Celtic Spirit, who has shown some form on Good but is 0-for-8 on Standard, faces a surface concern that makes this scenario fragile.

watchPoints.text: The Bay Warrior has not raced for 67 days — watch the market move and early paddock behaviour to assess whether the layoff is a fitness risk or a freshness advantage going into a race he can control.

With Muy Muy Loco, Haveagobeau, Celtic Spirit, and Saliko all holding natural hold-up profiles, watch for significant crowding and traffic problems in the straight as multiple closers chase the same limited gaps in a field of only seven.

Lady Of Clover is the most interesting hold-up runner given her Standard-going wins at 12f — watch her positioning in the early stages; if she can sit just off midfield rather than stone last, she could prove best-placed of the closers.

Celtic Spirit wears a hood (hg:p) for the first time or as a change — watch for any change in early racing behaviour, as horses switching headgear on AW can show an unpredictable early response that disrupts the expected race shape.

Boston Run is trained by Simon Dow alongside Muy Muy Loco — stable has 1 win from 9 runners over 14 days; if Ghiani elects to press The Bay Warrior rather than sit off, this could turn into a two-horse lead battle that plays into the hands of Lady Of Clover and the closers.
